title: Existing proper Serre-heart input: continuous
statement: Fix a prime ℓ and a field k with ringChar(k) ≠ ℓ. Let Y be a Noetherian k-scheme with structure map aY and p:Z→Y a proper morphism. For a commutative condensed ring Λ, write A_T for ordinary module objects over its pullback to T and R p_*:D(A_Z)→D(A_Y) for total right derived pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let S_Z be the smallest class of A_Z containing constructible modules and closed under isomorphisms, kernels, cokernels, extensions and coproducts indexed in Type (u+1). Then ProperLowerStarHeartHypotheses(Λ,p) means: there exists d∈ℤ such that R p_*(M[0]) is at most d for every M∈S_Z, and for every such small family (M_j) in S_Z the canonical map ⊕ R p_*(M_j[0])→R p_*(⊕ M_j[0]) is invertible. Let E be a normed field with a NormedAlgebra structure over ℚ_ℓ and finite dimension over ℚ_ℓ, and Λ=C(-,E). Then ProperLowerStarHeartHypotheses(Λ,p) holds.

proof.text: The proper heart theorem gives a uniform finite upper bound and direct-sum continuity on ind-constructible modules. In the integral case obtain the constructible bound from the derived reduction tower: the torsion bound is 2d and its Milnor limit costs one degree; pass to ind-constructibles by bounded-below filtered continuity. In the rational cases use the rational heart bound, including finite-coefficient descent for the condensed algebraic closure. The source formulation permits arbitrary finite extension presentations, not only a particular embedded presentation.

The ind-constructible class contains constructibles and is replete and closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions and ambient sums. Minimality therefore puts the constructible Serre coproduct closure inside it. Restrict both the heart upper bound and the canonical coproduct comparison to this subclass. Empty sums, zero modules and empty fibres are included.
